cards.text: Picture it, friend. Tattenai, a governor, has written to King Darius asking him to check whether King Cyrus ever approved rebuilding the house of God in Jerusalem (Ezra 5:6-17). So Darius orders a search of the archives stored in the treasury of Babylon.

cards.question: Darius has the archives in Babylon searched for Cyrus's decree. Where does the scroll turn up?

cards.text: Ecbatana, in the province of Media. Friend, I lived in a junk drawer, so I've SEEN this: you tear the whole kitchen apart for the scissors, and they're in the OTHER drawer.

cards.question: The scroll is a memo about a decree King Cyrus issued in his first year. Cyrus says to rebuild God's house in Jerusalem as a place for offering ___.
Cyrus's memo even gives the size of God's house: sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide. True or false: the Jews have to pay the building costs themselves.

cards.text: There's one more thing in that memo. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken things from the temple in Jerusalem and carried them off to Babylon.

cards.question: Cyrus's memo says the things Nebuchadnezzar carried off to Babylon must go back to the temple in Jerusalem. What are they?

cards.text: So Darius has his answer, and he writes back to Tattenai, Shethar-bozenai and their officials. Those are the men who went asking the Jews who authorized all this building (Ezra 5:3-4).

cards.question: King Darius writes to Tattenai, the governor who questioned the Jews about the building. What's the first thing Darius tells him?

answers.text: Stop the work until I come

cards.text: Darius keeps going: "Leave this work on the house of God alone." And the cost? Paid in full from the royal treasury.

cards.question: Darius says the building costs come from the royal treasury, out of the taxes of the provinces west of the ___.

cards.text: Tattenai's own region's taxes are now paying the BILL, friend. And Darius isn't done, because he's got a whole list for the priests too.

cards.question: Darius also orders young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings, plus wheat, salt, wine and oil, whatever the priests in Jerusalem request. They get it ___ without fail.
True or false: Darius says all these supplies let the priests offer sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the lives of the king and his sons.

cards.text: The king's covering the supplies, and he's like, while you're up there, put in a word for me and the boys. Then he adds a warning for anyone who interferes with this decree, and friend, this king does NOT mess around.

cards.question: Darius warns that anyone who interferes with his decree will be impaled on a beam torn from his own house. And what happens to the house?

answers.text: It becomes a pile of rubble

cards.text: Then come Darius's words about God: "May God, who has caused His Name to dwell there…"

cards.question: Darius's words: may God overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter this decree, or to do what?

cards.text: Then he signs off: "Let it be carried out with diligence." That box is SEALED, friend.
Now it's Tattenai and Shethar-bozenai's move, friend. King Darius has spoken, so what do they do?

cards.question: True or false: Tattenai and his associates diligently carry out what King Darius decreed.

cards.text: Like the coworker who questioned your whole project suddenly carrying the boxes for you. And with that, the Jewish elders build, and they prosper.

cards.question: The Jewish elders build and prosper through the prophesying of two prophets. Who are they?
With Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesying, the elders finish building according to the command of the ___ of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of ___.

cards.text: And then, friend, it happens. The house of God is finished. DONE. COMPLETE. Not almost done. DONE.

cards.question: The temple is completed on the third day of the month of Adar. In which year?

answers.text: The sixth year of King Darius
The first year of King Cyrus

cards.text: The priests, the Levites and the rest of the exiles celebrate the dedication of the house of God with joy. That's me when a whole tray comes out of the oven perfect, except their reason is a WHOLE lot bigger than cookies.

cards.question: For the dedication they offer a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, plus a sin offering for all Israel of twelve male goats. Why twelve?

answers.text: One for each tribe of Israel
One for each month of the year
One for each gate of Jerusalem

cards.text: With the house dedicated, it's time to get everybody organized. The priests go by their divisions and the Levites by their groups, for the service of God in Jerusalem.

cards.question: True or false: the priests and Levites are organized for the service of God according to King Darius's decree.

cards.text: It's according to what is written in the Book of Moses. Then on the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles keep the Passover.

cards.question: Before the Passover, what had all the priests and Levites done?
The ___ slaughter the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their priestly brothers and for themselves.

cards.text: Then comes the Passover meal. After all that building, friend, everybody's ready to eat.

cards.question: True or false: only the Israelites who returned from exile eat the Passover.

cards.text: All who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD eat with them. Then for seven days, they keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy.

cards.question: The people keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy. Where does that joy come from?

cards.text: The LORD had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel. The house of God is standing again, friend, and no, I'm not crying, I just got flour in my eye.

findings.problem: Card 5 calls the scroll "Cyrus's memo," and card 7 does too. The text calls it a memorandum that records a decree Cyrus issued: "Memorandum: In the first year of King Cyrus, he issued a decree." It is written about Cyrus in the third person. It is not Cyrus's own memo. Card 4 words this correctly: "a memo about a decree King Cyrus issued."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Nebuchadnezzar is introduced as "king of Babylon," which is a fact from outside Ezra 6. The card gives no reference for it. Ezra 5:12 supports it. Card 1 does cite its outside context (Ezra 5:6-17), so this card should too.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke "Tattenai's own region's taxes are now paying the BILL" only works if the baker knows Tattenai governs the region west of the Euphrates. No card ever says this. Card 1 calls him only "a governor," and card 8 never names his region. So the baker can't connect the provinces in card 11 to Tattenai.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from the passage. It cites Ezra 6:13, but it only restates that Darius has spoken and asks what Tattenai and Shethar-bozenai do. None of 6:13 is actually told.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Blank 2, "kings of ___" (Persia), can't be reasoned out. No earlier card says Cyrus or Darius rules Persia. They are only "King Cyrus" and "King Darius." Meanwhile, the earlier cards named Babylon (the treasury) and Media (where the scroll was found), so those two wrong answers look just as likely as the right one.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Babylon" for "kings of ___" is one a baker could argue is right. Ezra 5:13 calls Cyrus "king of Babylon," and the decree's archives were in Babylon.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "After all that building, friend, everybody's ready to eat" gives a reason the text doesn't give. It suggests they eat the Passover because they're hungry from building. The text only says they kept the Passover and ate it (Ezra 6:19, 21).

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "Everybody's ready to eat" hints at the answer to card 16 ("only the Israelites who returned from exile eat the Passover," which is False). It suggests more than the returned exiles ate, which helps rule out "True."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
